sections.title: Clinical Presentation: Observations
sections.content: Description: We can see in the first image that there is a left inferior dystopia with enophthalmos, left pseudoptosis, deep superior sulcus and right inferior eyelid retraction. Second image from below shows left enophthalmos or right proptosis. Third image of coronal CT scan shows left orbital floor defect with left maxillary sinus obliterated and smaller in size compared to the right one. Impression: traumatic enophthalmos due to orbital wall fracture.

sections.title: Examination Checklist
content: Complete ocular exam to exclude blunt trauma-related injury
VA, color vision, pupillary reaction, IOP

sections.title: Management Strategy
content: Step 1: Conservative management post-trauma to reduce edema and decrease diplopia.
Step 2: Evaluate for surgical intervention if enophthalmos > 2 mm.
Step 3: Surgical indications include persistent diplopia in primary gaze or cosmetically unacceptable enophthalmos.
Step 4: Surgical reduction of fracture with synthetic implant in collaboration with a maxillofacial surgeon.

sections.title: Clinical Pearl: Surgical Red Flags
content: Evidence of orbital fat herniation/muscle entrapment
